provenance.note: A felt-damped grand: a soft hammer low in the band, the brightness held under 2.6 kHz, a long two-stage fall and a second string barely detuned, so a chord blooms and stays round.

notes.copiedFrom: piano, its numbers changed for a soft keys backdrop; held at nought (AWAITING) until a part admits it
notes.timbres: none declared yet: the loudness fit measures a timbre when a part admits the row
notes.string: The deep house keys' string (round liquid-keys-2, his word 10-29 on the old grands the liquid keys draw: "yeah, that's the trick we might want to pull updated piano there as well"): the piano row's stiff string, wooden board and felt hammer in place of the six partials and the band of hiss, keeping this row's own envelope, lid (brightMin and brightMax), unison and high-pass, with the grand body, a gentle stiffness, the string reaching half as high on a hard strike, and a darker, longer felt (300 Hz, 26 ms) at its 0.05 hammer. Its `register` is its level by register against this row's six partials, measured note by note (MIDI 36-88, velocities 0.5 and 0.6, 3 s from the strike, dry): every register plays as loud as it did, the mean difference under 0.55 dB.
